stem:
Leela fills two upright plastic bottles with water. Bottle P is tall and narrow; the water surface is 30 cm above a side hole near the base. Bottle Q is short and wide; it holds more water in total, but its water surface is only 12 cm above an identical side hole.

She opens both holes at the same time.

parts.text: Which claim about the water pressure at the holes is correct?

options.text: Pressure is greater at P's hole because the water column above it is taller.
Pressure is greater at Q's hole because Q holds more water in total.
A taller water column produces lower pressure at the hole.
Pressure at the two holes must be equal because both bottles hold water.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Liquid pressure at a depth depends on the height of the liquid column above that point, not on the total volume in a wider bottle.

teacher.key_rationale: Bottom pressure rises with liquid height. Total volume and width do not set the pressure when heights differ. Taller columns give higher, not lower, pressure.
